method: Static reverse engineering with rizin, Capstone, Ghidra, dnfile/dncil and PE/resource/archive inspection; no Windows sample was executed. atomscan slow scans and cleave facts were collected for every original.

samples.marker_line: Crackme-bound stealer: steals credentials; added concealed SQL

classifier.note: The shipped model leaves both malicious samples unflagged (lvl=-1, cls=0), despite added behavior coverage; no duplicate detections were added to manipulate classification.

samples.identification: Unattributed native C++ multi-store credential stealer bound to a genuine crackme decoy; counterfeit Windows Update version resource.
packaging: Unsigned x64 GUI PE. CompanyName Microsoft Corporation, OriginalFilename WindowsUpdate.exe, product Microsoft Software Update.
An 11,554,332-byte overlay has entropy 0.0202; it includes substantial zero padding and an embedded approximately 20 KiB crackme. It is not uniformly one repeated byte.
execution_evidence: CRT enters 0x1400bf430. It creates a hidden --binder-child instance and invokes 0x140061eb0 to extract/start the bound decoy. The decoy main at 0x140001760 reads a candidate password, calls its checker and reports success/failure; its system call runs pause.

The wrapper invokes self-install routine 0x1400e7d90: resolves its own path and LOCALAPPDATA, creates a WindowsRecovery directory and Update.exe destination, copies/replaces its executable and registers HKCU Run through dynamically resolved registry APIs.

Main starts parallel Chrome, Firefox, Discord and wallet collection workers. Worker 0x1400b9070 calls Chromium collection; 0x1400bb180 schedules wallet collection; 0x1400b7090 gathers Discord tokens and submits an upload task.

0x1401ef620 opens browser databases, prepares and steps SQL, reads encrypted blob columns and invokes decryption helpers. Rolling-XOR strings decode to SELECT origin_url, username_value, password_value FROM logins and SELECT host_key, name, path, is_secure, is_httponly, expires_utc, encrypted_value FROM cookies.

0x1401f7a50 formats acquired cookie/login/token records and submits browser upload tasks. Native HTTP routines at 0x140043a10/0x140048b60 use dynamically resolved WinHTTP operations; this is not ordinary crackme functionality.

The program also contains a wallet ASAR modification path at 0x1400a6d00. Its recovered Electron snippet appends ignore-certificate-errors. This path was inspected but no broad ASAR-injection rule was added without a generalizable matcher for the modification relation.
obfuscation: Many strings are materialized into TLS storage with immediate stores.
Other strings XOR each input byte with a key updated as (key+index)&127. Initial keys may have their high bit set; both SQL matchers cover all 256 seeds.
Generic PE checks, CBC mode properties and memory-protection imports do not independently establish AES decryption or reflective loading.
samples.judgment_reason: Credential/token acquisition, upload workflows, self-installation, Microsoft impersonation and a bound password-challenge decoy establish malicious behavior. The external hostile provenance is consistent with the code.
samples.missing_context: No execution or live C2 transaction was performed. Delivery circumstances, operator and successful runtime exfiltration remain unknown.
samples.coverage: Two hostile findings cover credential harvesting and deceptive Microsoft identity; two suspicious findings preserve the distinct concealed password and cookie extraction queries. Existing wallet-target, file/process, crypto and structural detections are retained.

samples.marker_line: Rust HTTP implant: remote tasks/injection; added XOR/shim traits

classifier.note: The shipped model leaves both malicious samples unflagged (lvl=-1, cls=0), despite added behavior coverage; no duplicate detections were added to manipulate classification.

samples.identification: Unsigned custom Rust HTTP command implant with Early Cascade and remote-thread injection; not established as Sliver.
packaging: Native x64 console PE, implant.pdb CodeView basename, no Authenticode signature.
Contains ureq/3.4.2 HTTP/TLS code and embedded trust anchors. Certificate CRL URLs in that trust store are not C2 endpoints.
execution_evidence: CRT main thunk 0x140028080 reaches 0x14001a2c0. It initializes host identity/configuration, polls for work, sleeps between attempts and has failure/retry termination handling.
Configured external host is 191.44.66.129. The configuration also reconstructs http://191.44.66.129 using XOR 0x2b, uses a Chrome-like User-Agent and /api/v2/telemetry and /api/v2/status route text.

0x140011130 performs the task-poll/request/JSON-processing path; runtime command handlers include native process execution, filesystem and registry operations, CLR-hosted assembly loading, file upload and process injection.

0x1400101e0 opens a supplied file and constructs a multipart transfer including hostname, source_path and file. It feeds the configured HTTP transport. The decoded failure diagnostic explicitly refers to sending the file to C2, but that diagnostic is not used as a sample-specific detection.
0x1400278a0 opens the supplied process with 0x1fffff rights, allocates remote RW memory, writes supplied bytes, computes the entry point, changes protection to 0x40 and starts CreateRemoteThread.

0x14001c410 creates a suspended child, allocates/writes payload memory, finds NTDLL through the PEB, scans loader code for the two shim-global signatures, writes an encoded callback and enables shims with a one-byte write, then resumes execution. The WPM sequence is at 0x14001d0fd/0x14001d145.

0x1400139f0 hosts CLR v4.0.30319 and uses SAFEARRAY/COM assembly-loading and invocation interfaces. An AMSI-failure diagnostic exists, but no AMSI patch was established; an AMSI bypass is not claimed.
obfuscation: 0x14004ea90 copies source bytes XORed with a supplied key and validates the resulting text. Scalar loop 0x14004ebab and vectorized branches are present.
Task metadata and many diagnostics use this keyed string concealment. APIs are partly dynamically resolved.
samples.judgment_reason: Configured external tasking plus arbitrary execution, file-transfer and stealth injection capabilities make this a likely malicious implant on a machine. Its name and corpus label are corroboration, not the basis of the verdict.
samples.missing_context: Authorized red-team use is possible, but no operator authorization or deployment context was supplied. Runtime success and server ownership were not tested.
samples.coverage: Three suspicious findings cover concealed diagnostics, concealed remote-thread injection capability and Early Cascade shim-signature/remote-write APIs. The last matcher does not itself bind a computed shim address to the write destination, so suspicious is used despite the confirmed hostile-capable implementation. No fabricated extra hostile behavior was added to reach a count.

samples.marker_line: ieo PDF preview installer: upstream match; consented Drive access

classifier.note: Unflagged model output agrees with the evidence-based benign judgment.

samples.identification: ieo Windows WebView2 PDF-reader preview installer, product release 0.1.2-preview; unsigned .NET Framework application.
packaging: Unobfuscated IeoPreviewInstaller IL and embedded Payload ZIP plus Manifest JSON; high .text entropy is primarily compressed resources.
Every declared file size/hash and the payload archive SHA-256 verified. The exact outer executable was fetched from the developer preview download and matched the requested SHA-256.

The three WebView2 DLLs match Microsoft.Web.WebView2 1.0.3967.48 from NuGet byte for byte, including their existing signature bytes. This is an upstream byte comparison, not an independent Authenticode chain-verification claim.
The PDF.js worker and 200 asset files match pdfjs-dist 6.4.299 byte for byte.
execution_evidence: Installer Main prompts for installation/removal, writes versioned files under the current account, validates extracted member paths against traversal, validates hashes, creates desktop/Start-menu shortcuts and registers its own uninstaller.

Installer only updates an existing Run value whose path and arguments match its own installation. It does not enable startup on a new installation. Uninstall only deletes the matching own Run value and preserves reading data/program versions for rollback.
Ieo.Native.StartupRegistration.Set is called from the settings message handler to implement the user startup choice. It refuses conflicting unrelated values.

ieo-native.exe hosts the reader in WebView2. https://ieo.example/ is a virtual origin mapped to bundled local assets, not a remote callback. The bridge only accepts the expected top-level origin and dispatches a finite set of application settings/OAuth/Picker messages.

Google sign-in uses a default-browser OAuth/PKCE flow and a loopback listener with state checks. Native token/identity requests use Google endpoints; frontend synchronization uses Google Drive file/appdata scopes for the consenting account.

Refresh authorization is stored with Windows CurrentUser DPAPI; access authorization remains in memory. Local profile, migration, reading-library and QA paths were reviewed. No browser credential harvesting, arbitrary remote command dispatcher or third-party exfiltration destination was found.
retrievals: https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client (403; retrieval failed, retained as a documented limitation)
samples.judgment_reason: The recovered installer and app implement their stated PDF-reading/optional Drive-sync purpose, with user-facing consent and constrained own-application installation/startup operations. Verified upstream distribution and dependency bytes support BENIGN.
samples.provenance_explanation: The original source submission circumstances are unknown. The named antivirus results are generic/ML labels. An unsigned recent preview, compressed high-entropy managed resources, COM shortcut creation and Run/Uninstall registry operations plausibly account for those heuristics; this is an inference, not proof of why it was submitted. Corpus provenance alone does not establish an extra hostile payload.
samples.missing_context: The Google client script returned 403 to forager. Live account authorization/Drive operations were not exercised. A BENIGN marker is the requested quarantine-routing judgment, not a claim of independently established ground-truth benignness.
samples.coverage: No hostile/suspicious findings fire in the outer installer or manually extracted payload scan. Accurate notable registry, crypto, archive, COM, reflection, file and application capability observations remain. The extracted ZIP scan covers 23 analyzed units (members plus decoded layers), unchanged before/after.

shared_corrections.change: Same matcher, scope, exclusions and consumers; suspicious to notable, with a neutral capability name and placement. CBC mode properties prove neither AES nor decryption; unrelated PE checks and protection APIs do not bind data to executable loading. Every exact consumer reference was updated. No ancestor-directory consumers were found.
Same generic CodeView basename detection, retained at notable. Family identity and unrelated infrastructure ATT&CK attribution removed. No exact/broad consumers of the generic rule were found.
Same size/entropy matcher, same notable level and exclusion; accurate size/entropy name replaces unsupported uniform single-byte filler claim. Its consumer reference was updated.

verification.outside_batch_result: All prior non-third-party findings retained; no newly introduced suspicious/hostile findings on benign controls. Baseline materialized from HEAD; third-party additions in current fixture reports are excluded from relocation comparison because that baseline snapshot contains only the four YAML tiers.
verification.behavior_loss: No supported behavior was lost in any original or checked external fixture. The old loader interpretation, Sliver association and uniform-filler claim were unsupported; their accurate underlying observations remain.
verification.final_check_required: make validate (run after this report and all judgment markers are written)
